item.title: Dolly Parton, country music legend, dies at age 80
item.description: Dolly Parton became an icon over her six-decade career as a Grammy-winning singer-songwriter, movie and TV star and theme park owner who donated millions to help others.

item.title: Trump orders flags at half-staff to honor Dolly Parton after her death
item.description: President Trump on Tuesday said he is lowering the American flag throughout the U.S. following the death of legendary singer-songwriter Dolly Parton. CBS News' Anthony Mason, Jamie Wax and Nicole Valdes have more.

item.title: Watch Live: Prosecutors in Lindsay Clancy trial call final witness

item.title: Dolly Parton's nephew announces her death in social media video
item.description: Dolly Parton, legendary singer-songwriter, actress and philanthropist, has died at 80. Her nephew announced her death on Tuesday in a video on social media. CBS News' Anthony Mason and Jamie Wax have more.

item.title: Dolly Parton said "the town tramp" inspired her iconic look | 60 Minutes Archive
item.description: 60 Minutes' Morley Safer spoke to Dolly Parton back in 2009 about her iconic look and how being underestimated helped her in business. Parton died at 80, her family announced Tuesday.

item.title: From 2012: Dolly Parton on writing "I Will Always Love You" and Whitney Houston connection
item.description: Dolly Parton, the legendary singer-songwriter, actress and philanthropist, has died at 80, her family says. She spoke to CBS News' Rebecca Jarvis in 2012 about her song "I Will Always Love You," which Whitney Houston turned into a global phenomenon with her rendition for the "The Bodyguard" soundtrack. "She just took it worldwide and made it the most special song in the whole world for a long period of time," Parton said.

item.title: At least 1 in 4 ex-NFL players who died from 2016 to 2021 had CTE, study finds
item.description: At least 25% of ex-NFL players who died between 2016 and 2021 had chronic traumatic encephalopathy, or CTE, a study released Tuesday showed. Dr. Robert C. Cantu, founding member and medical director for the Concussion and CTE Foundation, joins CBS News to discuss.

item.title: ICE releases father of U.S. Navy sailor serving on USS Abraham Lincoln
item.description: Luis Manuel Aviles Roa, the father of a U.S. Navy sailor onboard the USS Abraham Lincoln, was released by ICE on Tuesday, his family told CBS News.

item.title: Legal breakdown of testimony about religion in Lindsay Clancy trial
item.description: Closing arguments are expected this week in Lindsay Clancy's murder trial for the killings of her three young children. Attorney and legal analyst Joe Tamburino joins CBS News to discuss the case and a moment on Monday where witness testimony was cut short over comments about religion.

item.title: CIA Director John Ratcliffe on secret trip in Russia
item.description: A U.S. Air Force Boeing C-17A Globemaster III transport plane was spotted at a Moscow airport, along with a U.S. diplomatic motorcade, according to public reports.

item.title: Texas Gov. Abbott refuses to extradite ICE officer charged in Minneapolis shooting
item.description: Texas Gov. Greg Abbott, a Republican, is pushing back against Minnesota's attempt to extradite a U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement agent charged with shooting a Venezuelan man earlier in the year. CBS News' Camilo Montoya-Galvez reports.

item.title: Expert explains why Lindsay Clancy's religious beliefs have no legal weight
item.description: The judge in the murder trial of Lindsay Clancy denied a mistrial request from her attorneys but scolded the prosecution after a witness brought up Clancy's religious beliefs. CBS News' Shanelle Kaul reports, and legal analyst Joe Tamburino weighs in.

item.title: CIA Director John Ratcliffe on secret trip in Russia
item.description: CIA Director John Ratcliffe is in Moscow, Russia, for a round of meetings, sources told CBS News on Tuesday. The nature of the trip is unclear.

item.description: The charges against Major Jason Watson are believed by his attorneys to be among the only instances for officers of his rank in the history of the U.S. military to be charged under Article 88.

item.title: Mike Lindell withholds payment for recount request in Minnesota GOP governor primary
item.description: Mike Lindell is withholding the payment required for a recount and audit of ballots cast in the Republican primary for Minnesota governor, claiming that the Secretary of State's office has proposed an unlawful recount process, according to a statement released by his campaign Monday.

item.title: Gun-running ship located 78 years after being sunk by Israeli military
item.description: In June 1948, Israeli forces opened fire and sank the boat in waters off Tel Aviv on the orders of David Ben Gurion, Israel's first prime minister.

item.title: U.S. Air Force major criminally charged for criticizing Trump

item.title: A wife is accused of her husband's murder. Can she clear her name?
